title: Optimizing Database Performance with Covering Indexes
explanation: A covering index is a specialized database index that contains all the columns required to satisfy a specific query. When a query is executed using a covering index, the database engine retrieves the requested data directly from the index structure without performing a costly lookup against the underlying table data pages. This elimination of random disk I/O significantly reduces query latency and CPU utilization, particularly at high transaction volumes. Designing indexes to cover frequent query predicates and projections is a foundational technique for scalable relational database architecture.
takeaway: Design indexes to include all queried columns, eliminating expensive table lookups and accelerating query performance at scale.
author: Muhammad Junaeid
